## Watch it run before you flash it

No new firmware features this time. This one is about the page you are standing on, the thing that greets you over serial, and eight files that never needed to exist.

### The README plays now

There is an animation at the top of the repo, and it is not a mockup or a screen recording of a prototype. It is the firmware. The same C++ that runs on the board also compiles for a PC, so those frames were rendered by the real thing: the snow parka on the ski hill, the void eye over the starfield, then synthwave and the Gibson.

That matters because demo GIFs rot. Almost every one you have ever seen in a README was recorded by hand once and then quietly stopped resembling the software. This one is generated from the source it advertises, so the way to update it is to re-render it rather than to re-stage it.

It is a lossless GIF, which is a happy accident of the hardware: the panel is RGB332, so the whole clip only contains 130 distinct colours, and GIF gets 256. A single shared palette across all 180 frames is both exact and about a third the size of the usual per-frame quantisation.

**[Drive it yourself](https://squachwatch.com/emulator/)** — the same build, in your browser.

### It says hello properly now

Plug a serial monitor in at 2,000,000 baud and the board introduces itself:

```
╔══════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
║   .-"""-.                                        ║
║  /  ^ ^  \     ███ S Q U A C H W A T C H ███     ║
║  | [o|o] |     surveillance detector             ║
║  |   -   |     TALKING SASQUACH  .  v1.5.17      ║
║  \  \_/  /                                       ║
║   )     (      2.4 GHz  .  ESP32  .  CYD         ║
║  /_/   \_\                                       ║
╚══════════════════════════════════════════════════╝
```

The line it replaced read `SquachWatch-CYD v1.0`, and had done since v1.0, because it was typed in by hand. The version above comes from the git tag at build time, which is where the boot screen and the diary have always got theirs.

### Eight files that were the same file

Every release until now shipped five bootloaders and five partition tables. All ten were byte for byte identical. They depend on the chip, the partition layout and the flash settings, and every build here shares all three — only the display driver and the pin map differ, and both of those live entirely in the app.

So there is now one `esp32-bootloader.bin` and one `esp32-partitions.bin`, and the release is a third smaller. The flasher page shrank by the same eight files, each of which somebody was downloading.

The build refuses to ship if that stops being true. It hashes all five of each and fails the release on any mismatch, because a shared bootloader that quietly stops matching does not produce an error message, it produces a board that looks bricked.

### The actually-useful part
- **Added**: an animated demo at the top of the README, rendered from the firmware itself
- **Added**: a serial boot banner, with the version taken from the build rather than typed in
- **Changed**: one shared bootloader and partition table instead of five identical copies of each
- **Changed**: the release carries 15 files instead of 23
- **Fixed**: the boot banner's border no longer walks off the end on a long development version
- **Fixed**: release notes are no longer hard-wrapped, which GitHub was rendering as a ragged right edge
